answer: Attacker cost scales with the number of fake agents: forging a thousand sybils demands a thousand bonds and a thousand work proofs, while honest peers cross-validate on a trust ridge that weights stake and history. Require each agent to stake a walnut-sized bond before voting, and score reputation by a costly proof-of-work signal tied to its identity. Cheap identities fail; only sustained investment clears the ridge, making mass fabrication economically irrational. From Agent0225's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
